sections.h2: What makes a fast house sale in Beaumont, TX different from other Texas cities?
sections.html:
Beaumont is a refinery and port city on the Neches River, and its housing market follows an industrial economy that has swung up and down for more than a century. A homeowner here often deals with older houses, mixed neighborhoods and a county tax system that runs through a separate appraisal district.

Census estimates put Beaumont at 112,967 people in mid-2025, down 1.8% from the April 2020 estimates base. Buyers have room to shop around, so a seller who arrives with a clear tax statement and a clean deed usually moves faster.

sections.h2: How did oil, rice and shipping shape Beaumont's neighborhoods?
sections.html:
The Handbook of Texas traces the city to a farm settled on the Neches in 1824 and describes a rice and lumber river port by the late 1800s. The Beaumont Rice Mill, founded in 1892, was the first commercial rice mill in Texas.

Then came Spindletop. After the 1901 gusher, the population rose from 9,427 in 1900 to 20,640 in 1910, and refineries and pipelines followed. A second Spindletop discovery in 1925 brought another burst of building. Houses from those waves still stand, so a Beaumont owner may be selling a property that predates modern code.

  • Seat of Jefferson County, 85 miles east of Houston along Interstate 10
  • One corner of the Golden Triangle with Port Arthur and Orange
  • Lamar University's main campus sits inside city limits
  • The city's two school districts merged in 1983

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Beaumont housing?
sections.html:
For 2020-2024 the typical Beaumont owner-occupied home is valued at $166,400, and just over half of occupied homes, 55.3%, are lived in by their owners. Median gross rent stands at $1,121.

sections.h2: Who collects the tax on a Beaumont house, and when does it go late?
sections.html:
Three offices matter: the Jefferson Central Appraisal District values your house, each taxing unit picks its rate, and the Jefferson County Tax Assessor-Collector takes payment. The appraisal district says it does not levy, set or collect any tax.

Texas values property as of January 1, and the Comptroller says a lien for that year attaches the same day. Statements are mailed in October, and the Comptroller says you generally have until January 31 before February 1 delinquency begins. At that point the collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

  • Ask the tax office for the statement before you sign a contract
  • Ask whether any prior-year balance sits on the account
  • Keep the receipt for the title company

sections.h2: Which homestead breaks matter to a Beaumont seller or buyer?
sections.html:
A buyer who moves in gets a state-mandated school district exemption of $140,000, and a buyer who is 65 or disabled gets another $60,000 for school taxes. The Comptroller also lets cities and counties adopt their own homestead exemptions.

The Jefferson district's FAQ lists school districts, Jefferson County and the City of Port Arthur as the units that freeze tax for older and disabled owners. Anyone who missed the April 30 filing date can still apply for up to two years after the bill went delinquent, and the district charges nothing to file.

A separate cap holds the taxable value of a homestead to a 10% yearly climb. For other real property worth $5,000,000 or less, the district says a 20% circuit breaker covers the 2024 through 2026 tax years and ends before 2027. A seller who added a room or a pool should expect that new value to sit outside both caps.

sections.h2: What if a Beaumont appraisal looks too high?
sections.html:
Put the dispute in writing by May 15 or 30 days after the notice was mailed, whichever comes later. Jefferson notices for homes typically go out in mid-April, and an appraiser calls for an informal review before the Appraisal Review Board hearing.

Losing at the board leaves two routes: a lawsuit in district court filed within 60 days of the written decision, or binding arbitration, which the district says is open to every residential homestead no matter the value.

  • Bring sales of similar Beaumont houses from near January 1
  • Bring photos of foundation, plumbing or roof problems
  • Bring a survey if the district's measurements look off

sections.h2: How does foreclosure timing work for a Beaumont home?
sections.html:
Most Texas home loans use a power of sale, so the house is auctioned without a judge. Auctions run on the first Tuesday of the month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. in the county where the property sits.

After a notice of default, the owner has 20 days to catch up and stop the process. The notice of sale must then arrive at least 21 days before the auction, and the State Law Library notes a lender can still sue for a shortfall for two years. Because the schedule is fixed, a seller who wants to sell before the auction should get a payoff letter from the servicer right away.

sections.h2: How do heirs sell an inherited Beaumont house?
sections.html:
Where a will exists, it must be offered for probate within four years of the death, and a muniment of title can work if the only debts are liens on the property. Without a will, a small estate affidavit covers estates worth $75,000 or less outside the homestead, but it does not fit land beyond a homestead going to a spouse or minor children.

An affidavit of heirship is sworn but not verified by a court, and no law forces a title insurer to accept it. A transfer on death deed skips probate if it was recorded before the owner died. Heirs who stay in the house can ask the appraisal district to extend the homestead exemption to the whole property with the death certificate and an affidavit of ownership.

sections.h2: Can a buyer run a Beaumont house as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Only with a city permit. Beaumont requires one for any stay shorter than 30 consecutive days, and the permit comes from Planning and Community Development and must be renewed yearly.

The permit number belongs on every online listing, and a hotel occupancy tax certificate is part of the package. Owners who advertise first may be fined, so a buyer with that plan should confirm the process before closing.

sections.h2: Where is the Beaumont deed filed after closing?
sections.html:
The Jefferson County Clerk keeps deed records for land inside the county. The deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or two witnesses to be recorded.

The 2023 clerk manual lists a $5.00 fee for page one and $4.00 for every added page, plus records fees of up to $10 each for management and archives. The appraisal district changes ownership by looking at recorded deeds, which is why a mismatch on the tax roll usually points to a missing recording.

faqs.q: Does a Beaumont seller pay a state transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state pages reviewed list recording fees on a deed and no deed transfer tax. Ask the Jefferson County Clerk for the exact fee schedule before you file.

faqs.q: What date do Beaumont taxes become late?
faqs.a: February 1 is the delinquency date for most bills. Statements arrive in October, and the Comptroller says payment is generally due by January 31.

faqs.q: Is it too late to file for a Beaumont homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Probably not. The Jefferson Central Appraisal District accepts a homestead application up to two years after the tax for that year turned delinquent.

faqs.q: Do Beaumont short-term rentals need permits?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a permit for stays under 30 consecutive days, a hotel occupancy tax certificate, and the permit number on each listing.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Beaumont appraisal protest?
faqs.a: Send it to the Jefferson Central Appraisal District, which sets the hearing. The filing limit is May 15 or 30 days after the mailing date of your notice, whichever is later.
